title: GitHub Actions for Azure
description: Set up GitHub Actions workflows to build and deploy applications to Azure services.

data.text: GitHub Actions is a CI/CD platform built directly into GitHub. It uses workflow files written in YAML that live in the .github/workflows directory of your repository. Microsoft provides official actions for deploying to Azure.
A workflow is triggered by an event (push, pull request, schedule). Each workflow contains jobs, and each job runs on a runner (GitHub-hosted or self-hosted).

data.title: YAML - Deploy to Azure App Service with GitHub Actions
data.content: A basic workflow that builds a .NET app and deploys to Azure App Service.
data.code:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.x'
      - name: Restore dependencies
        run: dotnet restore
      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore
      - name: Test
        run: dotnet test --no-build --verbosity normal
      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: 'my-web-app'
          slot-name: 'production'
          publish-profile: ${{ secrets.AZUREAPPSERVICE_PUBLISHPROFILE }}
          package: '.'

terms.definition: A configurable automated process defined in a YAML file inside .github/workflows/.
A server that runs your workflow jobs. GitHub-hosted runners are VMs provided by GitHub with common tools pre-installed.
A reusable unit of code that performs a specific task. Microsoft publishes azure/webapps-deploy and many other Azure actions.

data.title: GitHub Actions Advantages
items: No separate service needed - workflows live in your repository
Huge marketplace of community and official actions
Free tier includes 2,000 minutes per month for public repos
Matrix builds let you test on multiple OS/runtime versions simultaneously

data.title: YAML - Matrix Build for Multiple Runtimes
data.content: Test your app on multiple .NET versions.
data.code:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        dotnet-version: ['7.x', '8.x']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: ${{ matrix.dotnet-version }}
      - run: dotnet test --no-build

data.title: Storing Secrets
data.text: Never hardcode credentials in workflow files. Use GitHub Secrets (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions) to store the Azure publish profile, service principal credentials, or any API keys.

data.title: Exercise: Create a GitHub Actions Workflow
data.description: Deploy a web app to Azure using GitHub Actions.
steps: Push a .NET web app to a GitHub repository
Add the workflow from the example above
Get the Azure publish profile from the Azure Portal
Add it as a GitHub Secret named AZUREAPPSERVICE_PUBLISHPROFILE
Push the workflow file and watch the Actions tab
data.expectedOutcome: A successful workflow run that deploys your app to Azure.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GitHub Actions workflows are YAML files in .github/workflows/
Microsoft provides official actions for Azure services
Store credentials in GitHub Secrets, not in workflow files
Matrix builds let you test across multiple configurations
data.takeaway: If your code is on GitHub, GitHub Actions is the most convenient way to build a CI/CD pipeline for Azure.
